standalone.label: Can be searched on its own
standalone.rule: The text identifies a named method/framework/dataset or a sufficiently specified conceptual question, without needing us to invent which unnamed study is intended. Searchable does not establish a unique source or a valid single-paper gold answer.
standalone.expectedBehaviour: Search the collection using the question; support the answer with clearly attributed sources. Ask about a version/setting if necessary.

topical_missing_context.label: Topic is useful, but intended study/system is missing
topical_missing_context.rule: Contains a substantive topic or methodological clue, but asks about the authors, a particular model, experiment, corpus or finding without identifying it. Plausible relevant passages can come from several studies.
topical_missing_context.expectedBehaviour: Use existing conversation if it resolves the reference. Otherwise ask a focused question about the topic/system/experiment or offer clearly distinguished source-specific findings.

generic_missing_context.label: Too general to identify the intended subject
generic_missing_context.rule: Asks about unnamed data, baselines, results, language, participants, settings or features with insufficient distinctive subject information. Explicit pronouns are not required: "What was the baseline?" also lacks its subject.
generic_missing_context.expectedBehaviour: Use prior conversation if available; otherwise ask what method, topic, experiment or result the user means. A document filename is not required.
